title: Three Winters and One Short Spoon
subtitle: 饮食健康 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 饮食健康（人与自我·生活与健康·饮食与健康）
meta: 主题语境：饮食健康（人与自我·生活与健康·饮食与健康）　|　核心词汇：flavour　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 flavour 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1963 my grandmother ① chose a flavour that no cook in the shop would have named, and she said the choosing was the whole of the winter. The ② flavour, meaning the taste itself and not the smell, ran three winters and stayed unnamed in the book; a flavour, she said, is the only thing in a shop that is judged by how long it is left unnamed.

Every ③ flavour in that shop had the same short spoon beside it, and the ④ flavour at the far counter, meaning the one they kept for the children and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A flavour, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to name; my grandmother said the naming is the part that fills three winters.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the flavour was the whole of the matter, meaning the character and not the taste. The ⑥ flavour, meaning the character and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody names; flavour, he said, is either something you choose or the only word that means both a taste and a character. He said the character is the part they remember.

By 1970 the ⑦ flavour had become a line in a plan, and the plan had become an argument about the short spoon. The ⑧ flavour of the whole thing, my grandmother wrote in January, was one shop and three winters of naming; flavour, she said, is either the one at the far counter or the reason you learned to name. She said the naming was never mentioned.

The ⑨ flavour I remember is the one named in the plan, which closed in 1972 and is still described as the quietest in the shop. A ⑩ flavour, my mother said in 1974, is the only one that improves by being named; every flavour, she said, is a character that has agreed to look like a taste. She said the character was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 味道；口味（指店里每一种旁边的那一种）
B. n. 味道（指那一种本身，与气味相对）
C. 固定搭配：choose a flavour 选一种口味
D. n. 口味（指留给孩子们的那一种）
E. n. 口味（抽象总称，指一家店铺的调味之事）
F. n. 口味（指计划里写到、被说出名字的那一种）
G. n. 韵味；特色；气氛（指一件事里人人都等却无人说破的那样东西）
H. n. 韵味（抽象总称，指人人都等却无人说破的那样东西）

items.q: chose a flavour that no cook in the shop would have named
The flavour, meaning the taste itself and not the smell
the flavour at the far counter
the flavour was the whole of the matter
the flavour had become a line in a plan
The flavour of the whole thing
A flavour, my mother said in 1974

answers.why: choose a flavour 意为“选一种口味”，1963 年祖母选了一种店里没有一位厨师肯说出名字的口味。
flavour 意为“味道”，指那一种本身而不是气味，它经过了三个冬天而在簿子上没有被说出名字。
flavour 意为“口味”，指店里每一种旁边的那一种，每一种旁边都有同一把短短的勺子。
flavour 意为“口味”，指留给孩子们的那一种，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
flavour 意为“韵味、特色、气氛”，指一件事里人人都等却无人说破的那样东西，叔叔说这份韵味就是那件事的全部。
flavour 意为“韵味”，指人人都等却无人说破的那样东西而不是那种口味，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
flavour 意为“口味”，指计划里写到、被说出名字的那一种，到 1970 年这一种成了计划里的一行。
flavour 意为“口味”，祖母一月写道，整件事的调味之事是一家店铺和三个冬天的说出名字。
flavour 意为“口味”，我记得的是计划里被说出名字的那一种，1972 年结束了，至今仍被说成店里最安静的一种。
flavour 为抽象总称，母亲 1974 年说，一种口味是唯一会因为被好好说出名字而变得更好的东西。
